name: Kusanagi flatter katana profile
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this pixel-art Kusanagi game sprite.
The user's correction is ONLY the blade outline: it is far too curved and resembles a scimitar. Make it look like a Japanese katana with ALMOST NO CURVE.
KEEP the canvas, the entire handle, gold guard, blue jewel, all blade colors and the overall sword length.
REPLACE the exposed blade geometry with a nearly straight strip: the TOP SPINE should run horizontally from the blue-jewel collar almost to the point. The lower cutting edge is parallel to the top spine for 90 percent of its length. There must be NO downward bow in the middle, NO rounded bulging belly, and NO tip curling upward. The last 10 percent is a SHORT STRAIGHT DIAGONAL BEVEL rising from the lower cutting edge to meet the top spine in an angular katana kissaki point. Only a tiny subtle overall sweep of about one native sprite pixel is acceptable.
The blade's width stays about five native pixels and total sword length about60 nativepixels. In this1983x793 source, blade begins aroundx535 with topedgey350 and bottomedgey490; keep these two edges nearly horizontal to aroundx1750, then close them with an angled point aroundx1900,y335. Specifically remove the current U-shaped sag in both edges and the high hooked tip. Keep the point at nearly the same height as the blade's base.
Preserve the pale-gold face, ochre upper edge, ivory lower edge, darkbrown outline and one small base rune. Preserve the white/paleblue/red hilt wrapping and blue gemstone. Coarse crisp pixel art consistent with this source, no added detail, glow, particles, text or other objects. Genuinely transparent RGBA background. One complete sword only.
source_pixels: Original generated RGBA image copied unchanged; fixed crop and nearest-neighbor sampling by compile_weapons.py.
